newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: MTBE Malaysia to optimise MTBE output in August.
newsitem.headline: MTBE Malaysia to optimise MTBE output in August.

text.p: MTBE Malaysia plans to produce more of the gasoline octane booster methyl tertiary butyl ether (MTBE) in August due to a slump in propylene prices, an industry source said on Wednesday.
"It is not really because of better MTBE prices, although they have improved," a source said. "It is because propylene has fallen by around $200 per tonne to the high $400s in the past two months."
The source said in comparison MTBE prices have been in the $250-$260 per tonne range although in the past weeks they have improved slightly.

MTBE Malaysia, a wholly owned subsidiary of state-owned Petronas, produces 300,000 tonnes of MTBE and 80,000 tonnes of propylene annually from its plant at Kuantan on the east coast of the peninsular.
But the plant can vary the output of each product from between 100 percent to 80 percent of capacity depending on market conditions.
Propylene is a petrochemical which is processed further to produce polypropylene which in turn is used in the plastics industry to make tapes, bottles, film and fibre.
The source said the plant has been running on high-propylene mode since the begining of the year when propylene price went on a bull run with the shutdown of a large polypropylene plant in Libya.
"The Libyan plant is back now and is offering cargoes," the source said.
